definition: A Latin abbreviation for 'et uxor,' meaning 'and wife.' It is a traditional legal shorthand used in court documents and case names to indicate that a married couple is joined together as parties in a lawsuit, without listing the spouse's full name separately in the title.
examples: In the case title 'Joel Frederic, et ux.,' the 'et ux.' refers to Joel Frederic's wife, Elizabeth Frederic, who is also a plaintiff in the lawsuit against the Missionaries.
